newsitem.title: UK: Vickers warns of lower profits in Q1, H2.
newsitem.headline: Vickers warns of lower profits in Q1, H2.

text.p: British engineering group Vickers Plc said on Thursday its first-quarter profits were below last year's level, indicating that half-year results would not match year-ago figures.

"Export orders -- and let me remind you that in recent years Vickers has exported on average about 50 percent of our UK turnover -- are proving harder to obtain, and profit margins on them tend to be thinning," chairman Sir Richard Lloyd told shareholders.
Vickers' shares fell more than six percent after the news, dropping 14.5 pence to 211.5 by 1120 GMT.
The maker of Rolls-Royce cars and Challenger tanks had previously warned that this year's performance could be dragged down by sterling's strength, which has hurt many British exporters.
"We see 1997 as a year of consolidation," Lloyd said.

"But we are confident that the significant investments which we have made will positively impact results, and that over 1997 and 1998 taken together, the growth pattern for your company will be sustained," he added in a statement from the annual general meeting.
As previously reported, Lloyd said first-quarter sales of Vickers' Rolls-Royce and Bentley cars rose 13 percent to 446 versus the year-ago period. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
